answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond in a scarce resource before it may vote or claim rewards; a registry records the bond’s unique transaction, preventing one deposit from backing many accounts at once. Honest agents recover it after a nadir of inactivity or a lantern-lit audit, while identities caught coordinating fraud forfeit it. The attacker must therefore lock up real capital for every fake identity, risking that capital as the network checks behavior; cheap account creation alone no longer buys influence, even if the bond is ivory-colored in the interface.
